---
title: "Corridor segments"
format: html
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false

library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(leaflet)

epsg_code <- 32635  # UTM zone 35N

corridor <- st_read("../data/generated/corridor.gpkg")
waterway <- st_read("../data/generated/waterway.gpkg")
streets <- st_read("../data/generated/streets.gpkg") |> 
    filter(highway %in% c("motorway", "primary", "secondary")) |> 
    st_geometry() |> 
    st_transform(epsg_code)
```

A couple of utility functions:

```{r}
# query the Overpass API for a key:value pair within a given bounding box
osmdata_as_sf <- function(key, value, bb){
    bb |>
        opq() |>
        add_osm_feature(key = key, value = value) |>
        osmdata_sf()
}
```

```{r}
# get geometry in lat/lon (WGS84)
getGeomLatLon <- function(x) st_transform(x, 4326) |> st_geometry()
```

3. Corridor segments

Get intersections between the main street network and the riverline:

```{r}
crossings <- st_intersection(streets, waterway)
```

Note that the segmentation algorithm below can also be used as an alternative to cap the ends of the corridor. In this case, the crossings of the ring road seem to match the original delineation quite well.

```{r}
leaflet() |>
    addTiles() |>
    addPolylines(data = streets |> getGeomLatLon(), color = "black", opacity = 100, weight = 1) |>
    addPolylines(data = waterway |> getGeomLatLon(), color = "blue") |>
    addPolylines(data = original_delineation |> getGeomLatLon(), color = "green") |>
    addPolylines(data = corridor |> getGeomLatLon(), color = "yellow") |>
    addCircles(data = crossings |> getGeomLatLon(), color = "red", fill = "red", radius = 10)
```
